grammar_concept.title: Verb + Gerund vs. Verb + To-Infinitive
grammar_concept.rule: Some verbs are followed by a gerund (verb+ing): enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest. Other verbs are followed by a to-infinitive: want, decide, promise, need, hope. There is no simple rule for which is which — you need to learn each verb's pattern.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Depois de certos verbos, o verbo seguinte tem de ficar em -ing (gerúndio); depois de outros, tem de ficar com "to" (infinitivo). Não há uma regra simples — aprende-se caso a caso, verbo a verbo.
grammar_concept.example: I enjoy reading before bed. I want to travel next year.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Gosto de ler antes de dormir. Quero viajar no próximo ano.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português, a maioria dos verbos equivalentes usa o infinitivo ("gosto de ler", "quero viajar"), o que leva falantes de português a usar sempre "to" + infinitivo em inglês também: dizem "I enjoy to read" em vez de "I enjoy reading". Alguns verbos em inglês (enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest) exigem obrigatoriamente o gerúndio, nunca o infinitivo com "to".
grammar_concept.correction: Não existe atalho: é preciso decorar o padrão de cada verbo. Os mais comuns com gerúndio: enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest, keep, practise. Os mais comuns com to-infinitivo: want, decide, promise, need, hope, plan, agree.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Numa conversa: "I'm thinking about changing jobs, but I haven't decided to leave yet."

vocabulary.definition_en: to try not to do something, or to stay away from something
example_sentences: I avoid eating late at night.

vocabulary.definition_en: to say an idea for someone to consider
example_sentences: She suggested going to the cinema.

vocabulary.definition_en: to do something regularly in order to improve a skill
example_sentences: I practise speaking English every day.

exercises.explanation: "Enjoy" é sempre seguido de gerúndio (-ing), nunca de "to" + infinitivo.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: "I enjoy to read" é um erro muito comum, por transferência direta do português.

exercises.explanation: "Want" é seguido de to-infinitivo ("to travel"), nunca de gerúndio.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar o gerúndio ("travelling") depois de "want" é um erro comum, misturando o padrão de outros verbos.

correct_answer: to try not to do something, or to stay away from something
exercises.explanation: "Avoid" é seguido de gerúndio: "avoid doing something".

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the doctor suggest?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "My doctor suggested changing my diet."
exercises.transcript: My doctor suggested changing my diet. I've decided to try it, even though I don't enjoy cooking very much.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "I practise speaking English every morning. I've also decided to watch films without subtitles, even though I sometimes avoid difficult ones." What has the speaker decided to do?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "decided to watch films without subtitles".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Ela sugeriu experimentar o novo restaurante."
correct_answer: She suggested trying the new restaurant.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "to try" depois de "suggest" ("suggested to try") é um erro comum.

steps.content: In fast, casual speech, "want to" often reduces to something close to "wanna" /ˈwɒnə/ — you'll hear this a lot, but it's not used in writing or formal contexts.

steps.prompt: Talk about 3 things you enjoy doing and 3 things you want to do this year, using the correct gerund or infinitive for each verb.
Write 5 sentences using enjoy, avoid, suggest, want and decide correctly (gerund or to-infinitive).
